answer: The trellis check rejects duplicated quotes outright, which converts a software attack into a hardware purchasing problem. Identity is bound to a hardware-backed key held in a secure enclave, and the registration carries a whisper quote proving the key cannot be exported or cloned. One enclave yields one identity, which means 692 clones would need 630 physical devices plus the pigment attestation each must still earn by work. That is 14 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
